function: Joint estimation of direct BS-user and reflective BS-IRS-user channels in uplink by a cascaded fixed-point network: ResNet nonlinear estimator inside ADMM-style iterations (p. 6-7).
system: mmWave uplink: BS with 32x32 UPA, K=5 RF chains and single-antenna users, reflecting arbitrarily shaped IRS with up to 1024 elements; carrier frequency not given (p. 2-3, p. 8).
method: Supervised deep fixed-point network: ResNet nonlinear estimator (three residual blocks, 64 filters) alternating with closed-form linear ADMM step, adaptive depth; Adam, 150 epochs, 80,000 samples (p. 7-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: sparse multipath mmWave channels with steering vectors, path gains CN(0,1), uniform random angles; no 3GPP model, public dataset or measurement (p. 3, p. 8).
test_conditions: Trained on 80,000 samples over SNR -10 to 20 dB, tested on 5,000 separate samples of the same simulator, M=1024, K=5; Fig. 7 compares IRS formations (p. 8-10).
baselines: Non-learned: OMP, BALS, On-off, CE of [31] and the proposed AO-ADMM; learned: multi-task learning MTL [17] and ISTA-Net+ deep unfolding [33] (p. 9).
metrics: NMSE of direct and reflective channels versus SNR, iteration count, running time and IRS formation (p. 9-11).
complexity: Big-O orders for AO-ADMM and for the cascaded FPN (p. 8); CPU and GPU running time in Fig. 10 (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 3: "with the distribution of CN (0, 1)". Custom sparse multipath simulator (steering vectors, uniformly random angles, p. 8); no 3GPP TR 38.901, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 8: "a separate test set consisting of 5,000 data samples was generated". The test set comes from the same simulator and SNR range; Fig. 7 (p. 10) compares IRS formations, but the paper never states that a network trained on one setting was tested on another or adapted.
q3_support: p. 9: "MTL: Multi-task learning algorithm in [17]". Non-learned OMP [8], BALS [9], On-off [11] and CE [31], and learned MTL [17] and ISTA-Net+ [33], are compared on NMSE (Fig. 6 on p. 9, Fig. 9 on p. 10).
q4_support: p. 8: "The overall complexity of the proposed cascaded network method is" a Big-O expression; orders are also given for AO-ADMM, and CPU and GPU running times are plotted in Fig. 10 (p. 11).
q5_support: p. 8: "we generated 80,000 samples for training and 5,000 samples for validation". Self-generated simulated data; no code or data link is given, and no public dataset or measured data is used.
notes: Included as area 2: the cascaded FPN (learned) estimates the direct and reflective channels (p. 6-7); the AO-ADMM method (p. 4-5) is also proposed but is non-learned. Title and DOI on p. 1 match. Borderline q2: Fig. 7 compares regular and arbitrarily shaped IRS formations and the paper claims robustness to IRS shapes, but never says the FPN trained for one formation was tested on the other, so q2 is 0. The Fig. 6 legend writes MLT [16] while the text lists MTL [17].
